name: Practice Fusion
description: Practice Fusion is a cloud electronic health record and billing platform for independent medical practices. Practices use it for charting, patient records, e-prescribing, scheduling, labs and imaging, secure referrals, reporting, patient engagement, and connected billing workflows.
agentUseSummary: Practice Fusion is visible as a developer-review preview only. Relay will not collect a Practice Fusion login, token, client secret, patient portal credential, patient identifier, chart, prescription, insurance detail, payment detail, or other credential, and no agent action is callable until Practice Fusion and Relay's healthcare owners approve the exact bounded read-only FHIR contract.

capabilities.label: Read approved Practice Fusion clinical summaries
capabilities.description: After Practice Fusion and Relay's healthcare owners approve the integration, read only bounded patient- or practice-authorized FHIR summaries for one exact practice, limited to explicitly approved resources and fields.

blocked.label: Connect before developer approval
blocked.description: Practice Fusion requires developer registration, applicable API terms and fees, implementation details, base URLs, and provider approval. Relay has no registered FHIR application, approved practice contract, healthcare compliance acceptance, or production access.

blocked.label: Collect clinical or application credentials
blocked.description: Relay will not ask for a Practice Fusion login, token, client secret, patient portal credential, patient identifier, chart, prescription, insurance detail, payment detail, or other secret as a substitute for approved authorization.

blocked.label: Run Practice Fusion API actions
blocked.description: No patient, appointment, chart, medication, allergy, vital, order, result, billing, message, export, or other Practice Fusion API action can run while developer and healthcare review is pending.

blocked.label: Clinical and financial mutations unavailable
blocked.description: Proprietary bi-directional APIs, chart changes, scheduling, prescriptions, orders, billing, messaging, bulk exports, raw PHI, and every mutation remain outside Relay's planned read-only V1 even after approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Practice Fusion developer review pending
approvalProfiles.description: Clinical reads remain unavailable until developer registration, API terms and fees, production authorization, privacy, security, practice approval, and healthcare compliance are accepted.

runtimeSupport.description: No OpenClaw tools are callable until Practice Fusion approves Relay and Relay implements the approved read-only Railway broker.
No Hermes tools are callable until Practice Fusion approves Relay and Relay implements the approved read-only Railway broker.

providerSetup.blocker: Practice Fusion documents uni-directional FHIR APIs and separate proprietary bi-directional APIs. Its FHIR guide requires developer registration and directs developers to third-party application terms, applicable API fees, implementation details, authorizations, tokens, resources, bulk exports, and service base URLs. Relay has no registered application, accepted terms or fees, approved authorization contract, practice sponsorship, BAA and HIPAA allocation, minimum-necessary resource map, security acceptance, or production access.
providerSetup.nextAction: Authorized Relay business, legal, privacy, security, healthcare compliance, and product owners must register the exact developer application, accept applicable API terms and fees, obtain practice sponsorship and production approval, and document the minimum-necessary read-only FHIR contract. They must define authorized practices and users, exact resources and minimized fields, consent and purpose limitation, token and base-URL discovery, tenancy, audit, retention, deletion, breach duties, limits, disconnect, and production acceptance. Engineering can then implement a fixed-origin Railway broker for only approved bounded clinical-summary reads. Proprietary bi-directional APIs, chart changes, scheduling, prescriptions, orders, billing, messaging, bulk export, raw PHI, and every mutation remain excluded.

evidence.supports: Practice Fusion publishes a FHIR developer guide, requires developer registration, references authorizations, tokens, resources, bulk export and base URLs, and points to third-party developer terms and applicable API fees.
Practice Fusion distinguishes simple uni-directional FHIR connections from proprietary APIs for custom bi-directional integration and describes a collaboration marketplace.
Practice Fusion identifies EHR 3.7 as ONC certified and links its FHIR APIs, certified API fees, export documentation, and required companion software.
Practice Fusion describes its EHR, billing, e-prescribing, patient engagement, and independent-practice workflows.
